content.content: The viewer applies each state change incrementally — touching only the elements the change affects — and applies pending changes to the surface at most once per frame.
content.rationale:
vztxmxum settles that an interaction's cost follows what it changed, not the number of nodes visible. This node records the mechanism that holds that relation: each state change — selection, hover, drag — is applied to the rendered surface by looking up and updating only the elements that change, and the changes pending within a frame are merged and applied once per frame. The account counts the whole cost of applying a change, from the arriving change through to what the surface ends up showing, and delegates no part of it to another decision. Nothing else is decided: no frame rate, latency budget, event-rate ceiling, rendering technique or library is named, and none is needed to apply it.

Use. Applying one change therefore costs work bounded by the elements that change — the element of the changed node or edge, its incident edges for a drag, the previously and newly emphasized elements for a selection or hover — and not by how many nodes and edges are rendered: the same change costs the same whether the panel shows few nodes or many. The saving is located in the reachability step below, not in timing: the once-per-frame rule bounds how often pending work is flushed, not how much work a change costs, so it is not a batching trick that would make the claim true by luck, and the account leans on no frame-rate or latency target. The bound covers the whole cost, including the surface work that produces the display, not only the writes the viewer itself performs.

Reachability. The affected elements are obtained from the element and adjacency maps the renderer already maintains — a change carries the identity of the node or edge it concerns, that key is looked up in the element map, and a node's incident edges come from the adjacency map — together with the currently emphasized set that the same bookkeeping already tracks. Nothing is discovered by reading, querying or rebuilding the surface: there is no whole-surface query, no traversal of rendered elements, and no step that asks the surface whether or how it changed.

Write scope. The update touches only the looked-up elements: a selection or hover rewrites emphasis on the previously and newly emphasized elements and nothing else, and a drag rewrites geometry on the dragged element and its incident edges. The surface as a whole is neither written, re-rendered, re-classed nor re-queried on the normal path, and there is no whole-surface fallback when a lookup misses — a missing entry ends that change and does not trigger a scan or a rebuild.

Per-event work. No step taken per incoming change, before or during coalescing, scans the visible nodes or edges or diffs the surface to discover what changed; a change is looked up and accumulated into the pending set, so the per-event work is proportional to the change and not to what is rendered.

Coalescing. Changes that land within one frame accumulate in a pending set keyed by element, so several changes to the same element merge into the pending entry rather than queuing duplicates, and the set is flushed at most once per frame. Nothing is dropped: correctness of the applied result depends on every pending change being merged and applied, not on any of them being discarded.

Full cost. The account does not stop at the writes the viewer performs; it covers the cost through to the displayed result. Because the update writes only the looked-up elements, the work the host does to present the result — its style recalculation, layout and paint — is confined to those written elements and the content those elements already carry, which is proportional to the changed element and not to how many nodes or edges are rendered. No step rewrites, replaces or restructures the document, rewrites a class or attribute on the surface root or on any container shared by the rendered nodes and edges, or otherwise invalidates the surface as a whole, so no host work is provoked that scales with the number of rendered nodes or edges. Every per-visible-node and per-visible-edge term that could enter between the arriving change and the display is therefore owned by this account; none is left out and none is assigned to another decision.

Consistency. No step on any path asserts or requires cost to grow with the number of rendered nodes or edges — not the lookup, not the write, not the coalescing, and not the host work that turns the written elements into the display; a step that would need such a quantity — a diff, a scan, a global class write, a document-wide invalidation — is excluded rather than merely bounded. The visible extent is whatever the surface happens to render at the time; it is not an input to any step of the mechanism.
